newsitem.title: USA: Electronic Designs sees price stability.
newsitem.headline: Electronic Designs sees price stability.

text.p: Electronic Designs Inc said Tuesady that it continues to see strong demand in its core memory module business from both the commercial and military sector.
The company said its volume is up 20 percent from a year ago, but that revenues have been adversely affected by the continued price weakness in the memory chip market.

"We have seen evidence of price stability returning to the memory market," said chief executive Don McGuinness, "and the company is increasingly optimistic that future unit volume increases will result in an increase in total revenues."

Net income for the second quarter of 1997 was $1.1 million, or $0.13 per share, versus $1.2 million, or $0.14 per share, for the comparable period in fiscal 1996. Revenues were $9.9 million for the second quarter of fiscal 1997, compared to $15.6 million in the year-earlier period.
The company also said that as a result of the three year ISO 9001 reaudit of its operations, its certification was extended to include display products.
ISO certification, said the company, will significantly expand market opportunities, both in the avionics retrofit market and in the original equipment manufacturers market.
